rules.title: Repeated SSH authentication failures
rules.summary: A source generated a concentrated authentication-failure burst against the controlled decoy gateway.

telemetryRequirements.purpose: Differentiate authentication failures from other controlled event types.
Correlate attempts to one lab source within the configured window.
Measure the bounded burst window without relying on arrival order.

investigationQuestions: Does one source meet the configured failure threshold within the correlation window?
Is a privileged username candidate present in the controlled event set?
triageGuidance.dispositionBoundary: Treat a threshold match as suspicious in the lab; use the known-benign scenario to verify that ordinary administrative access does not create a case.

expectedBenignCases: Scheduled service retries and users repeatedly entering an incorrect password.

severityGuidance.rationale: A concentrated burst against a lab decoy warrants analyst review.

riskScoreFactors.label: Failed attempts
riskScoreFactors.rationale: Failure count meets or exceeds the configured threshold.

riskScoreFactors.label: Source concentration
riskScoreFactors.rationale: Events are correlated to one source IP.

riskScoreFactors.label: Privileged targeting
riskScoreFactors.rationale: The event set includes a root account candidate.

rules.title: Successful login after repeated failures
rules.summary: A successful authentication followed a concentrated series of failures from the same source.

telemetryRequirements.purpose: Bind the failures and success to the same controlled source.
Confirm the transition occurs inside the defined correlation window.

investigationQuestions: Did the same lab source produce both the failure sequence and the later success?
Does the success remain inside the configured correlation window after the failures?
triageGuidance.dispositionBoundary: A successful login after mistakes can be benign; evaluate this rule alongside the benign-admin scenario and documented source context.

expectedBenignCases: A legitimate user can make several mistakes before successful authentication.

severityGuidance.rationale: Success after a concentrated failure sequence requires context.

riskScoreFactors.label: Prior failed attempts
riskScoreFactors.rationale: Previous failures were linked to the same source.

riskScoreFactors.label: Authentication success
riskScoreFactors.rationale: A login success followed the failure sequence.

riskScoreFactors.label: Temporal proximity
riskScoreFactors.rationale: The transition occurred within the configured correlation window.

rules.title: Multi-stage decoy engagement and discovery
rules.summary: Correlated credential activity, decoy engagement, and discovery-like behavior formed a complete lab attack story.

telemetryRequirements.purpose: Require the controlled credential, decoy, and discovery event categories.
Keep every stage attributable to one lab source.
Identify allowlisted discovery-like command evidence without storing raw TTY logs.
Validate stage order inside the bounded correlation window.

investigationQuestions: Are credential activity, decoy engagement, and discovery evidence all present for one source?
Do the observed discovery events meet the configured minimum without including raw session content?
triageGuidance.dispositionBoundary: Individual inventory commands are not sufficient; the critical lab story requires every configured stage and remains confined to controlled synthetic telemetry.

expectedBenignCases: Individual inventory commands without correlated credential activity should not trigger this rule.

severityGuidance.rationale: A full credential-to-decoy-to-discovery sequence is the highest-risk lab story.

riskScoreFactors.label: Credential activity
riskScoreFactors.rationale: The sequence begins with repeated authentication failures and a later success.

riskScoreFactors.label: Decoy engagement
riskScoreFactors.rationale: The source opened a controlled decoy session.

riskScoreFactors.label: Discovery sequence
riskScoreFactors.rationale: Discovery-like command events followed the session.

scenarios.label: Full pipeline story
scenarios.description: Brute-force attempts progress to decoy interaction and discovery behavior.

useCase.learningObjective: Validate that a correlated credential-to-decoy-to-discovery story continues to produce every intended detection after a rule or parser change.
validationSteps: Replay the controlled scenario from the analyst workspace.
Confirm that all three expected rules produce cases with one source-bound timeline.
Compare the observed rule IDs with the evaluation matrix before accepting the change.
useCase.expectedOutcome: Three detections are present: repeated failures, success after failure, and the multi-stage sequence.

scenarios.label: Credential probe
scenarios.description: Authentication failures followed by a successful login.

useCase.learningObjective: Practice deciding whether a later authentication success should be escalated by reviewing source continuity and the configured time window.
validationSteps: Inspect the failure and success evidence for one source and the defined correlation window.
Record a disposition that cites the triage boundary rather than the technique label alone.
useCase.expectedOutcome: Two detections are present and the case remains explainable as a lab signal that requires contextual review.

scenarios.label: Benign admin activity
scenarios.description: Normal administrative access that should not create a case.

useCase.learningObjective: Demonstrate that ordinary authorized administration and isolated inventory activity remain outside the current detection boundaries.
validationSteps: Confirm that the evaluation matrix reports zero observed detections and zero false positives.
Use the result as a negative control when revising a related correlation rule.
useCase.expectedOutcome: No case is created; the scenario remains a documented negative control.

scenarios.label: Threshold boundary
scenarios.description: Exactly one fewer authentication failure than the repeated-failure threshold.

useCase.learningObjective: Prove that the repeated-failure rule begins only at its declared threshold rather than alerting on nearby but insufficient activity.
validationSteps: Replay the edge-case scenario with one fewer failure than the configured threshold.
Confirm that no repeated-failure detection is observed.
Change the threshold only with a corresponding scenario and regression-test update.
useCase.expectedOutcome: No case is created, demonstrating a precise and testable correlation boundary.
